page: Microsoft Azure L2aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads. The compute configuration is supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. System memory totals 16.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Storage consists of a dedicated 1440 GB local NVMe SSD, and no GPUs are present.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-core performance alongside capacity limits inherent to a 2-vCPU configuration. In single-threaded assessments, the instance scored in the top 25%, achieving 2070.0 points in Geekbench single-core and 3076.98 in stress-ng. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics place in the lower quartile, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 2591.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3832.94. Memory bandwidth reaches 35.96 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 27.68 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific metrics show 2.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.31 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The qualitative value of the L2aos_v4 stems from its pairing of high local NVMe storage capacity with dedicated AMD EPYC compute. The high ratio of local NVMe SSD space to compute resources provides efficient density for disk-bound services that do not need broad multi-core parallelization. Workloads that match this profile include local caching layers, small transactional databases, log ingestion nodes, and data processing services requiring fast scratch space.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core processing capabilities, scoring in the upper 25% for Geekbench single-core and stress-ng tests. This configuration offers practical resource density for storage-intensive tasks that prioritize fast local NVMe read and write operations over heavy multi-core execution, such as caching nodes, log storage, and lightweight databases.
